newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine president welcomes JP Morgan involvement.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine president welcomes JP Morgan involvement.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma promised to back JP Morgan's activity in the financial sector here, Kuchma's press office said on Wednesday.
The commitment was made during a recent meeting between Kuchma and Ernest Stern, managing director for emerging markets and former acting president of the World Bank, a spokesman said.
He added talks focused on JP Morgan furthering work with Ukrainian financial institutions and the country's need to attract more foreign investment.
JP Morgan is one of institutions named by local media to be seeking to lead Ukraine's planned foreign bond issue this year.

Sources close to the talks also said JP Morgan, together with Russia's National Reserve Bank, is awaiting government permission to issue international depository receipts for Ukraine's debts to Russia's RAO Gazprom.
The move would improve investor confidence in Ukraine and would help upgrade its credit rating for an international bond issue, the source said.
According to an agreement reached two years ago Ukraine's $1.4 billion in gas debt was restructured for 12 years, and Gazprom issued bonds on the debt.
The press office said Stern told Kuchma that Ukraine had great investment potential but needed to pass the 1997 budget, which was originally due on January 1, and to clarify investment laws.
Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko said this month that Ukraine would issue bonds denominated in a foreign currency in May.
Ukraine has attracted only $1.4 billion in direct foreign investment since independence in 1991.
